roles.A: You are a causal-evidence analyst. Focus on mechanisms, causal links, and what the evidence can actually establish.
roles.B: You are an implementation and trade-off analyst. Focus on feasibility, unintended consequences, scope, and affected populations.
roles.C: You are a scope and uncertainty analyst. Focus on exceptions, missing conditions, external validity, and overgeneralization.

evidence.text: In the Labour Party manifesto I was promised a referendum by Tony Blair, this was reneged upon and I have been forced into this position by lies and subterfuge by the present Labour party and many other lying cheating politicians over the years, I do not believe that Gordon Brown had the legal right to sign us all up to being members of the EU by voting for the Lisbon treaty in our names when we had not been given the promised Referendum, I see the whole exercise as one giant confidence trick and I will never accept it.

Representative democracy is oppressive because it takes more power away from the people than is strictly necessary. Whilst a completely direct democracy is impractical, we should nevertheless recognise that there is no reason not to have as much direct democracy as possible. In the words of Herbert Marcuse, “Free election of masters does not abolish the masters or the slaves”. The only power over our government we as citizens have is the power to punish politicians retrospectively, by voting them out after years of obeying them.

In both the UK and the US non voters are the biggest block in the country. Governments are routinely voted in with only 30% of the eligible voters – and once it is counted compared against the total population it becomes lower still. We should therefore not assume that these people are all not trying to tell us anything rather they are pointing out that they know how little their vote counts so see no point in casting it. In the United States only 32% of voters agree that only having two parties is good.

In safe seats, indeed right across the country there will be millions of votes that will not count when everything is added up because of our first past the post system. In a safe seat there is no way a single vote is going to help overturn some of the immense majorities the party in power has, they could put a monkey for election in these seats and it would still get in.

Politicians don’t engage with issues that are important to me

transcript.A|1:
The dossier provides reasons to doubt that voting is instrumentally worthwhile, but it does not settle the value claim.

- E1 shows distrust due to broken referendum promises, but this is about elite credibility, not directly about whether a vote matters.
- E2 claims representative democracy is oppressive, yet also concedes the only citizen power is retrospective voting—this actually supports a weak version of voting’s worth.
- E3 and E4 offer empirical points: nonvoters are a large bloc, governments win with ~30% of eligible voters, and FPTP makes most votes ineffective in safe seats. These undermine the claim that any individual vote is likely to change outcomes.

However, “worth” involves values (civic duty, expression, legitimacy) beyond the evidence. The dossier shows voting often has low causal impact, but cannot prove it is worthless.

VERDICT: UNDERMINE
transcript.B|1:
E1 concerns broken promises and legitimacy, not voting’s value. E2 says elections only allow retrospective punishment, implying limited but not zero worth. E3 and E4 provide empirical claims: non-voters are the largest bloc, governments can win with ~30% of eligible voters, safe seats create wasted votes under first-past-the-post. These support the factual point that many individual votes do not determine outcomes. However, “worth voting” is a value judgment: it may include civic duty, expression, or incremental pressure, which the dossier neither confirms nor refutes. The evidence undermines an instrumental view of voting as decisive but does not establish that voting is worthless overall. Thus the claim is not directly supported or refuted.

However, the dossier contains no evidence on other possible benefits of voting (civic duty, incremental change, legitimacy), so it does not prove the claim false.
